meta.notes: Two adults + four kids (17, 15, and 9-year-old twins). Three weeks up and down the California coast finishing in Las Vegas. Fog in the mornings up north, desert heat down south — pack layers and sun cream. This whole plan works offline once installed, so don't panic when the signal drops in Big Sur or Death Valley.

legs.title: San Francisco
legs.tagline: Fog, hills and sourdough — easing in on the bay.
legs.notes: Five nights to shake off the jet lag. Mornings are foggy and cool right through August (Karl the Fog is real), so keep a layer in every bag even when it looks sunny. Parking is brutal — lean on cable cars, ferries and walking.

ideas.title: Alcatraz Island
ideas.note: Former island prison — the audio tour narrated by ex-guards and inmates is gripping. Pre-book, it sells out.

ideas.title: Walk or cycle the Golden Gate Bridge
ideas.note: Ride over to the harbour town of Sausalito, then ferry back with the bikes.

ideas.title: Ride a cable car
ideas.note: The Powell-Hyde line climbs past the Lombard Street zig-zags — hang off the side.

ideas.title: Fisherman's Wharf & Pier 39
ideas.note: Barking sea lions, sourdough bread bowls, street performers and arcades.

ideas.title: Exploratorium
ideas.note: Enormous hands-on science playground on Pier 15 — hours of fun, air-conditioned.

ideas.title: California Academy of Sciences
ideas.note: Aquarium, planetarium and a four-storey rainforest under one living roof (Golden Gate Park).

ideas.title: Muir Woods
ideas.note: Cathedral-quiet grove of giant redwoods, 30 min north. Parking/shuttle reservation required.

ideas.title: Painted Ladies, Alamo Square
ideas.note: The postcard row of Victorian houses with the skyline behind.

ideas.title: Chinatown
ideas.note: Oldest in North America — the fortune-cookie factory is a hit with kids.

ideas.title: Twin Peaks at sunset
ideas.note: The best panoramic view over the entire city; bring a layer, it's windy.

ideas.title: Mission District
ideas.note: The city's best burritos plus streets of colourful murals (Balmy Alley).

ideas.title: SF Giants baseball at Oracle Park
ideas.note: Waterfront ballpark — check whether the Giants are home during our dates.

days.title: Arrival in San Francisco
days.subtitle: Wheels down — a gentle first evening by the water.

options.title: Fisherman's Wharf & the sea lions
options.plan: Land at SFO, collect the rental car and check into the hotel. Once everyone's dropped their bags, take a slow stroll down to Pier 39 to see the sea lions barking on the docks — the perfect low-effort way to stay awake until a normal bedtime and beat the jet lag. Early night for everyone.
options.food: Clam chowder in a sourdough bread bowl at Boudin Bakery on the Wharf — a San Francisco rite of passage.

options.title: Ferry Building sunset
options.plan: If the flight's left everyone wired rather than wiped, wander the Embarcadero to the Ferry Building marketplace and watch the light go down over the Bay Bridge.
options.food: Grab tacos or a slice from the Ferry Building food hall and eat by the water.

tip.label: Book early
tip.body: Have all six passports and the car-hire confirmation to hand at the rental desk. Ask for the child booster seats you reserved — confirm them before you drive off.

days.title: Golden Gate & the bay
days.subtitle: The postcard day — bridge, bikes and Sausalito.

options.title: Cycle the bridge to Sausalito
options.plan: Hire bikes near the Wharf and ride the waterfront path out across the Golden Gate Bridge to the pretty harbour town of Sausalito (mostly flat, one big hill down into town). Mooch the galleries and waterfront, then let the ferry carry you — and the bikes — back to the city.
options.food: Fish and chips on the deck at Fish or Scoma's in Sausalito, watching the yachts.

options.title: Presidio & Baker Beach
options.plan: Drive to the Presidio, walk the Batteries-to-Bluffs trail and take the classic bridge photo from Baker Beach. Tunnel Tops park is superb for the twins to run off energy.
options.food: Picnic from the Presidio Tunnel Tops kiosks, or the Sessions food trucks.

options.title: Cable car & Lombard Street
options.plan: Ride the Powell-Hyde cable car (hang off the side!) up to Lombard Street's famous zig-zag, then down to Ghirardelli Square.
options.food: A hot fudge sundae at Ghirardelli — split a few, they're enormous.

tip.label: Layers
tip.body: The bridge is 10°C colder and windier than downtown, even in August. Everyone takes a jumper — no exceptions.

days.title: Alcatraz & the waterfront
days.subtitle: The Rock — history the kids will actually remember.

options.title: Alcatraz cruise & cellhouse tour
options.plan: Ferry out to Alcatraz for the excellent self-guided audio tour narrated by former guards and inmates — genuinely gripping for teens and 9-year-olds alike. Give it a good 2.5 hours on the island, then ferry back.
options.food: Lunch at the Ferry Building on the way back — build-your-own from the stalls keeps everyone happy.

options.title: The Exploratorium
options.plan: If Alcatraz is sold out (it books weeks ahead), Pier 15's Exploratorium is a giant hands-on science playground — hours of entertainment, and air-conditioned.
options.food: The Seaglass café on-site, or back to the Wharf.

tip.label: Book early
tip.body: Alcatraz tickets sell out weeks in advance — this must already be booked. Check the ferry departure time the night before; it leaves from Pier 33, not the Wharf.

days.title: Muir Woods & Marin
days.subtitle: Cathedral redwoods just over the bridge.

options.title: Muir Woods & Muir Beach
options.plan: Drive back over the bridge to Muir Woods and walk the boardwalk loop beneath 1,000-year-old coast redwoods — hushed, cool and jaw-dropping. Afterwards drop down to Muir Beach or the Muir Beach Overlook for the coastal view.
options.food: Pack a picnic (no big café at the woods), or the Pelican Inn at Muir Beach for a cosy English-pub lunch.

options.title: California Academy of Sciences
options.plan: Prefer to stay in town? The Academy in Golden Gate Park has an aquarium, planetarium and a four-storey indoor rainforest under one living roof. Brilliant for the twins.
options.food: The Academy café, or picnic in the park by the bandshell.

tip.label: Book early
tip.body: Muir Woods requires a parking OR shuttle reservation booked in advance — you cannot just turn up. No reservation, no entry.

days.title: City classics & pack-up
days.subtitle: Last of the city before the coast road.

options.title: Golden Gate Park, Painted Ladies & Twin Peaks
options.plan: A greatest-hits day: the Japanese Tea Garden and Stow Lake pedal-boats in Golden Gate Park, a photo at the Painted Ladies on Alamo Square, and a drive up Twin Peaks for the whole-city view at dusk. Repack tonight for the drive south.
options.food: A proper Mission burrito at La Taquería or El Farolito — the best-value dinner in the city.

options.title: Chinatown & North Beach
options.plan: Wander the oldest Chinatown in North America — the fortune-cookie factory is a hit — then over into Italian North Beach for cannoli and a rest in Washington Square.
options.food: Dim sum in Chinatown, then a cannoli at Stella Pastry in North Beach.

tip.label: Prep the drive
tip.body: Fuel up tonight and download offline maps for Monterey → Big Sur — signal disappears on the coast road. Everything in this app already works offline.

legs.title: Pacific Coast Highway
legs.tagline: The drive is the destination — Big Sur, cliffs and elephant seals.
legs.notes: Four days threading Highway 1 down the coast. The road itself is the main event: hairpins, sea cliffs and pull-offs. Phone signal is patchy to non-existent through Big Sur — screenshot anything you need, and trust this app, which runs fully offline. Fill the tank whenever it drops below half.

ideas.title: 17-Mile Drive
ideas.note: Scenic private toll road past Pebble Beach and the lone cypress.

ideas.title: Bixby Creek Bridge
ideas.note: The iconic Big Sur photo stop — pull off just before it.

ideas.title: McWay Falls
ideas.note: An 80ft waterfall dropping onto a cove beach; short easy walk to the overlook.

ideas.title: Pfeiffer Beach
ideas.note: Purple-tinged sand and a sea arch, down a narrow hidden lane.

ideas.title: Point Lobos Reserve
ideas.note: Gentle cliff trails, tide pools and sea lions — good for the twins.

ideas.title: Monterey Bay Aquarium
ideas.note: World-class; the sea-otter feed and kelp forest are unmissable.

ideas.title: Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk
ideas.note: Old-school seaside rides — the wooden Giant Dipper coaster is a scream.

ideas.title: Hearst Castle
ideas.note: Opulent hilltop mansion with Roman pools; timed tour bus from the visitor centre.

ideas.title: Elephant seal rookery, Piedras Blancas
ideas.note: Hundreds of enormous seals on the beach a few metres from a free boardwalk.

ideas.title: Morro Bay
ideas.note: Kayak the calm bay beneath the giant 176m Morro Rock.

ideas.title: Lunch at Nepenthe
ideas.note: Cliff-top terrace 800ft above the Pacific — arrive early or book.

days.title: San Francisco → Monterey
days.subtitle: The coast road begins — otters and aquarium.

options.title: Monterey Bay Aquarium & Cannery Row
options.plan: Drive south (roughly 2 hours) to Monterey. Spend the afternoon at the world-class Monterey Bay Aquarium — the kelp forest and sea-otter feeds are unmissable — then stroll the old sardine canneries of Cannery Row.
options.food: Clam chowder and calamari on Old Fisherman's Wharf, Monterey.

options.title: Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk
options.plan: Break the drive at Santa Cruz for the old-school seaside boardwalk — the wooden Giant Dipper coaster is a scream and the twins can ride all afternoon.
options.food: Corn dogs and funnel cake on the boardwalk — full holiday mode.

tip.label: Fuel up
tip.body: Fill the tank in Monterey before you head into Big Sur tomorrow — there's one very pricey petrol station on the whole stretch and long gaps between.

days.title: 17-Mile Drive & Big Sur
days.subtitle: The big one — cliffs, bridges and hidden beaches.

options.title: Bixby Bridge, McWay Falls & Pfeiffer Beach
options.plan: The signature day of the trip. Loop the 17-Mile Drive past the Lone Cypress, then take Highway 1 into Big Sur proper: stop at the iconic Bixby Creek Bridge, walk to the McWay Falls overlook (a waterfall onto the beach), and detour down to purple-sanded Pfeiffer Beach. Drive slowly, stop often.
options.food: Nepenthe for lunch — famous cliff-top terrace with a view a thousand feet above the Pacific. Book or arrive early.

options.title: Point Lobos walk
options.plan: Swap some driving for the gentle cliff trails of Point Lobos Reserve — tide pools, sea lions and hidden coves, easy enough for the twins.
options.food: Picnic at Point Lobos, or back into Carmel-by-the-Sea for lunch.

tip.label: No signal
tip.body: There is essentially zero phone reception through Big Sur. This day's page is built to work with no connection at all — screenshot any bookings and go. Watch for fog on the cliff bends.

days.title: Big Sur → Cambria
days.subtitle: Castles on the hill and seals on the sand.

options.title: Hearst Castle & the elephant seals
options.plan: Continue south to San Simeon. Take the tour bus up to Hearst Castle — the jaw-dropping hilltop mansion with its Roman pools — then stop at the Piedras Blancas rookery just up the road, where hundreds of enormous elephant seals lounge on the beach a few metres away. Overnight in Cambria.
options.food: Dinner on Moonstone Beach in Cambria, or a Main Street bistro in the village.

options.title: Morro Bay & the Rock
options.plan: Skip the castle tour for the laid-back fishing town of Morro Bay, dominated by its 176m volcanic Morro Rock. Kayak the bay or just watch the otters.
options.food: Fish tacos on the Morro Bay Embarcadero.

tip.label: Book early
tip.body: Hearst Castle tours must be booked in advance and depart on a strict timetable from the visitor centre — you can't just walk up to the house.

days.title: Cambria → Santa Monica
days.subtitle: The American Riviera, then down to the beach base.

options.title: Santa Barbara stop, then push to Santa Monica
options.plan: Break the drive at Santa Barbara — the whitewashed, red-tiled 'American Riviera'. Walk out on Stearns Wharf and mooch State Street, then tackle the final run down to your Santa Monica base for the next four nights.
options.food: Lunch on Stearns Wharf or at the Santa Barbara Public Market.

options.title: Solvang Danish village
options.plan: Swing inland to Solvang — a slightly surreal Danish-themed village of windmills and bakeries. Kitsch, fun, and great for photos.
options.food: Aebleskiver (Danish pancake balls) at a Solvang bakery.

tip.label: Beat the traffic
tip.body: LA traffic builds through Sunday afternoon. Aim to clear Santa Barbara by mid-afternoon so the last stretch into Santa Monica stays sane.

legs.title: Santa Monica
legs.tagline: Beach base — pier lights, bikes and Pacific sunsets.
legs.notes: Four nights parked by the beach. Everything here is walkable or a short cruiser-bike ride, so the car can mostly stay put. The classic beach-path runs all the way from Santa Monica to Venice — use it.

ideas.title: Santa Monica Pier & Pacific Park
ideas.note: Solar-powered Ferris wheel and coaster right over the ocean.

ideas.title: Cycle the beach path to Venice
ideas.note: Flat 3.5km each way; hire cruiser bikes for the whole stay.

ideas.title: Venice Beach boardwalk & Muscle Beach
ideas.note: Skaters, street performers and the famous outdoor gym — peak people-watching.

ideas.title: Venice Canals
ideas.note: A quiet, pretty walk over little bridges — a total contrast to the boardwalk.

ideas.title: Abbot Kinney Boulevard
ideas.note: Trendy boutiques, murals and arguably the best casual food in LA.

ideas.title: Beginner surf lesson
ideas.note: Mellow breaks and instructors used to kids — everyone stands up eventually.

ideas.title: Malibu beaches (El Matador)
ideas.note: Sea caves and arches up the coast; small car park, go early.

ideas.title: Third Street Promenade
ideas.note: Open-air shopping street with buskers, a few minutes from the pier.

ideas.title: Getty Villa
ideas.note: Roman and Greek antiquities in a stunning re-created villa (free, book ahead).

ideas.title: Original Farmers Market & The Grove
ideas.note: Historic food stalls next to an open-air shopping district.

days.title: Santa Monica Pier & beach
days.subtitle: Roller coaster over the ocean.

options.title: Pacific Park & a proper beach day
options.plan: Ease into LA with a full beach day. Ride the solar-powered Ferris wheel and coaster at Pacific Park on the pier, hire umbrellas and bodyboards, and let the twins loose in the sand. Sunset over the Pacific from the pier is the reward.
options.food: Burgers and shakes at a pier-side spot, or the historic Santa Monica food stalls.

options.title: Bike the beach path to Venice
options.plan: Hire cruiser bikes and ride the flat 3.5km beach path south to Venice and back, stopping wherever looks good.
options.food: Poke bowls or tacos on the Venice side.

tip.label: Beach kit
tip.body: Rent beach cruisers for the whole family for the four days — cheaper by the day and it turns the whole coast into your back garden.

days.title: Venice & Abbot Kinney
days.subtitle: Skaters, canals and one very odd boardwalk.

options.title: Canals, skate park & Abbot Kinney
options.plan: Explore the peaceful Venice Canals (yes, real canals with little bridges), watch the pros at the Venice Skate Park, take in the chaos of the boardwalk, then wander the boutiques and murals of hip Abbot Kinney Boulevard.
options.food: Abbot Kinney has the best casual food in LA — take your pick of the trendy spots or the original Venice pizza joints.

options.title: Family surf lesson
options.plan: Book a group beginner surf lesson on the mellow Santa Monica or Venice breaks — instructors are used to kids and everyone stands up eventually.
options.food: Well-earned brunch back on Main Street, Santa Monica.

tip.label: Keep it loose
tip.body: Venice Beach gets eccentric — brilliant for people-watching, but keep the twins close on the boardwalk and valuables zipped away.

days.title: Universal Studios Hollywood
days.subtitle: Movie-world day trip.

options.title: Universal Studios Hollywood
options.plan: A big day out at Universal: the Studio Tour tram through real backlots, the Wizarding World of Harry Potter, Super Nintendo World and Jurassic World. Something for the 9s, the teens and the grown-ups. Get there for opening.
options.food: Eat inside the park — Three Broomsticks in Hogsmeade is the fun choice.

options.title: The Getty Center
options.plan: Not up for a theme park? Ride the tram up to the Getty Center for world-class art, extraordinary architecture and gardens, and one of the best views over LA — and it's free to enter.
options.food: The Getty's restaurant and café, with a view.

tip.label: Book early
tip.body: Buy dated Universal tickets online in advance and consider the Universal Express pass — August queues are long. Rope-drop the Studio Tour first.

days.title: Malibu day
days.subtitle: Hidden coves up the coast.

options.title: El Matador, Malibu Pier & Point Dume
options.plan: Drive up the coast to Malibu's string of beautiful state beaches. El Matador's sea caves and arches are the showstopper (steep steps down), Point Dume is great for a scramble and whale-spotting, and Malibu Pier is the classic photo stop.
options.food: Fish tacos at a Malibu beach shack, or a bite at the Malibu Country Mart.

options.title: Third Street Promenade & chill
options.plan: A gentler day: shopping and street performers on Santa Monica's Third Street Promenade, then back to the beach. Good if everyone needs a slower gear.
options.food: Take your pick on the Promenade — every cuisine going.

tip.label: Parking
tip.body: El Matador's car park is tiny and fills by late morning. Go early, or be ready to wait for a space. Pack water — there are no shops at the beach.

legs.title: Los Angeles
legs.tagline: Hollywood, theme parks and the big-city stretch.
legs.notes: Five nights to take on LA proper. It's vast and the traffic is real — plan each day around one area and travel outside peak hours. This is the leg where the four kids' different tastes pull hardest, so a couple of days are built to split the group.

ideas.title: Hollywood Walk of Fame & TCL Chinese Theatre
ideas.note: The stars, the handprints and the tourist buzz of Hollywood Blvd.

ideas.title: Griffith Observatory
ideas.note: Free space museum, telescopes, and the definitive Hollywood Sign view at sunset.

ideas.title: Universal Studios Hollywood
ideas.note: Harry Potter, Super Nintendo World, Jurassic World and the backlot Studio Tour.

ideas.title: Disneyland / California Adventure
ideas.note: The original Disney parks, down in Anaheim — a full magical day.

ideas.title: Six Flags Magic Mountain
ideas.note: One of the biggest roller-coaster line-ups on the planet — the teenagers' day.

ideas.title: The Broad
ideas.note: Modern art incl. Yayoi Kusama's Infinity Mirror Rooms — free, but book timed tickets.

ideas.title: La Brea Tar Pits
ideas.note: Bubbling Ice Age tar pits and a museum of sabre-tooths and mammoths, mid-city.

ideas.title: Getty Center
ideas.note: Art, gardens, architecture and huge city views — free (pay for parking).

ideas.title: Warner Bros. Studio Tour
ideas.note: Behind real working film and TV sets — brilliant for film-mad teens.

ideas.title: Rodeo Drive & Beverly Hills
ideas.note: Window-shopping and people-watching in the famous zip code.

ideas.title: LA Dodgers at Dodger Stadium
ideas.note: Classic MLB night out — check whether they're home during our dates.

ideas.title: Griffith Park & LA Zoo
ideas.note: Huge park with a zoo and a vintage train museum — space for the twins to roam.

days.title: Hollywood
days.subtitle: Stars on the pavement, sign on the hill.

options.title: Walk of Fame & Griffith Observatory sunset
options.plan: Do the Walk of Fame and the handprints at the TCL Chinese Theatre in the morning, then time the afternoon for Griffith Observatory — the best free view in LA, a superb space museum, and the definitive Hollywood Sign photo as the sun drops.
options.food: Dinner in Los Feliz below the observatory, or the classic In-N-Out for the full American road-trip experience.

options.title: Warner Bros. Studio Tour
options.plan: For film-mad teens, the Warner Bros. Studio Tour goes behind the scenes of real working sets and prop houses — Friends, Batman, the lot.
options.food: Lunch on the studio lot or in nearby Burbank.

tip.label: Beat the crowds
tip.body: Griffith Observatory parking fills fast at sunset. Arrive well before golden hour or use the DASH shuttle — and bring a layer for after dark.

days.title: Disneyland
days.subtitle: The big one for the twins.

options.title: Disneyland Park, Anaheim
options.plan: A full day at the original Disneyland. Rope-drop the headliners (Rise of the Resistance, Space Mountain, Indiana Jones), pace it with breaks, and stay for the fireworks over the castle. A long but magical day — the twins will talk about it for years.
options.food: Eat in the park; the Galactic Grill in Tomorrowland or a Dole Whip in Adventureland are easy wins.

options.title: Disney California Adventure
options.plan: The sister park across the plaza — Avengers Campus, Cars Land and the Guardians drop tower skew a bit older, so it can suit the teens better.
options.food: Pym Test Kitchen in Avengers Campus is a laugh.

tip.label: Book early
tip.body: Disneyland needs dated tickets AND a park reservation. Download the Disneyland app and set up Lightning Lane / Genie+ the night before to skip the worst queues.

days.title: Griffith Park & museums
days.subtitle: A gentler recovery day after Disney.

options.title: LA Zoo & Griffith Park
options.plan: A deliberately easier day after Disneyland. The LA Zoo and the vintage Travel Town train museum in Griffith Park are perfect for tired twins, with plenty of shade and space to roam.
options.food: Picnic in Griffith Park, or a casual lunch in nearby Los Feliz.

options.title: The Broad & Downtown
options.plan: For the older four, The Broad museum downtown (Yayoi Kusama's Infinity Mirror Rooms are the draw) plus the striking Walt Disney Concert Hall next door.
options.food: Grand Central Market downtown — dozens of food stalls under one roof.

tip.label: Book early
tip.body: The Broad is free but timed-entry tickets go fast, and the Infinity Rooms need a separate reservation. Sort it a few days ahead.

days.title: Six Flags Magic Mountain
days.subtitle: The teenagers' day — serious coasters.

options.title: Six Flags Magic Mountain
options.plan: Aimed squarely at the 15- and 17-year-olds: Magic Mountain has one of the biggest roller-coaster line-ups on the planet. A great day to split the group — thrill-seekers here, twins and a grown-up back at the beach or the hotel pool.
options.food: Park food, or refuel in nearby Valencia on the way back.

options.title: Beach & pool day
options.plan: The other half of the family takes it easy — Santa Monica beach in the morning, hotel pool in the afternoon. Everyone reconvenes for dinner and swaps stories.
options.food: Family dinner back near the hotel — somewhere everyone's voted for.

tip.label: Split the group
tip.body: Height limits keep the twins off most of Magic Mountain's big rides, so splitting the day is kinder to everyone. Agree a pickup time and place before you separate.

days.title: Getty, Beverly Hills & desert prep
days.subtitle: Culture, glamour, and stocking up for Nevada.

options.title: The Getty & a Beverly Hills stroll
options.plan: Ride the tram up to the Getty Center for art, gardens and views, then a stroll down Rodeo Drive for the Beverly Hills people-watching. A cooler, calmer day — and the last chance to stock the car before the desert.
options.food: Lunch at the Getty, or a deli in Beverly Hills.

options.title: La Brea Tar Pits
options.plan: Bubbling Ice Age tar pits right in the middle of the city, with a museum full of sabre-tooth cats and mammoths dug from the asphalt. A quirky, kid-friendly winner.
options.food: The Original Farmers Market at 3rd & Fairfax is a short hop and full of options.

tip.label: Desert prep
tip.body: Buy a case of water and check the car's air-con works properly before tomorrow — you're driving into serious August heat. Charge everything tonight.

legs.title: Las Vegas
legs.tagline: Neon, desert wonders and one last blow-out.
legs.notes: Four nights to finish in the desert. August in Nevada is brutally hot (40°C+) — plan outdoor stuff for early and late, and hide from the midday sun in the air-conditioned casinos and pools. Hydrate constantly, especially the kids. The Grand Canyon and Death Valley pages are built to work with no signal at all.

ideas.title: The Strip after dark
ideas.note: Bellagio fountains, the neon, and free casino spectacles all the way down.

ideas.title: High Roller observation wheel
ideas.note: 550ft views over the valley — spectacular by day or night.

ideas.title: Gondola ride at The Venetian
ideas.note: Indoor and outdoor canals with singing gondoliers — kitsch and fun.

ideas.title: Adventuredome at Circus Circus
ideas.note: Indoor theme park — the perfect way to dodge the midday heat.

ideas.title: Grand Canyon West / Skywalk
ideas.note: The big day trip — glass walkway out over the void. Leave at dawn.

ideas.title: Hoover Dam
ideas.note: Walk across the colossal dam and the bypass bridge, 45 min from the Strip.

ideas.title: Death Valley
ideas.note: Otherworldly desert — Badwater Basin and Zabriskie Point. Extreme heat; prep well.

ideas.title: Seven Magic Mountains
ideas.note: Stack of giant neon-painted boulders 20 min south — a quick, fun photo.

ideas.title: Fremont Street Experience
ideas.note: Old-town Vegas: canopy light show, buskers and a zipline overhead.

ideas.title: Red Rock Canyon
ideas.note: Scenic 13-mile loop drive through red sandstone, 30 min from the Strip.

ideas.title: A family show
ideas.note: A Cirque du Soleil production or a big magic show — book ahead.

ideas.title: Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium
ideas.note: NFL under the dome — check whether they're home during our dates.

days.title: Los Angeles → Las Vegas
days.subtitle: Across the Mojave into Nevada.

options.title: Drive to Vegas & the Strip by night
options.plan: The roughly 4.5-hour drive across the Mojave to Las Vegas. Break it at the retro ghost town of Calico or the tiny outpost of Baker (home of the world's tallest thermometer). Check in, cool off, then hit the Strip after dark for the Bellagio fountains and the neon.
options.food: One of the famous Vegas buffets, or an easy Strip diner — the kids will be wide-eyed either way.

options.title: Death Valley crossing
options.plan: For the adventurous: route via Death Valley National Park — Badwater Basin (lowest point in North America), Zabriskie Point and the dunes. Spectacular and utterly alien, but only with a fully fuelled, well-watered car.
options.food: Stock up before you enter — services inside the park are minimal and far apart.

tip.label: No signal
tip.body: Fuel up and load the car with water before leaving LA. The Death Valley option in particular has long stretches with no reception and 45°C+ heat — this page works fully offline. Never leave anyone in a parked car.

days.title: The Strip
days.subtitle: Family-friendly Vegas, believe it or not.

options.title: High Roller, fountains & Adventuredome
options.plan: There's plenty for kids on the Strip: ride the High Roller observation wheel, gawp at the Bellagio fountains and the Venetian's canals and gondolas, raid M&M's World and the giant sweet shops, and burn off energy at Circus Circus's indoor Adventuredome. Free casino spectacles everywhere you look.
options.food: Grab a table at one of the themed restaurants — the Venetian's food hall or a Strip pizzeria keeps everyone happy.

options.title: Pool day
options.plan: It's 40°C+ — sometimes the answer is the hotel pool all day. Most Strip resorts have huge pool complexes with lazy rivers and slides. Save the Strip for the cool of the evening.
options.food: Poolside snacks, then a proper dinner out once the sun's down.

tip.label: Heat plan
tip.body: Do the outdoor Strip walking early morning or after sunset; take the middle of the day indoors. Refill water bottles everywhere and slap on the sun cream — desert sun is fierce even for a short walk.

days.title: Grand Canyon or Hoover Dam
days.subtitle: One of the great wonders — worth the early start.

options.title: Grand Canyon West day trip
options.plan: The big finale excursion. Grand Canyon West (about 2.5 hours from Vegas) is the closest rim, home of the glass Skywalk jutting out over the void, plus Eagle Point and Guano Point viewpoints. Set off at dawn to be back for a last Vegas evening.
options.food: Lunch at the Grand Canyon West ranch, or pack a hamper for the drive.

options.title: Hoover Dam & Lake Mead
options.plan: Prefer a shorter day? The colossal Hoover Dam is only 45 minutes out — walk across the dam, take the power-plant tour, and cross the bridge for the classic view. Add a Lake Mead viewpoint on the way back.
options.food: Lunch in Boulder City, the sweet little town that built the dam.

tip.label: Early start
tip.body: The Grand Canyon is a long day in the heat — leave before sunrise, take far more water than you think you need, and keep an eye on the kids near the (largely unfenced) rim edges.

days.title: Departure — flying home
days.subtitle: Three weeks done. Wheels up.

options.title: Last breakfast, return the car, fly home
options.plan: A relaxed final morning: pack, one last American breakfast, top up the fuel and return the rental car, then to Harry Reid International (LAS) in good time for the flight home. Sleep on the plane — it's an overnight back to the UK.
options.food: A final proper American breakfast — pancakes, bacon and unlimited coffee.

options.title: Seven Magic Mountains photo
options.plan: If the flight's later, the Seven Magic Mountains — a stack of giant neon-painted boulders 20 minutes south of the Strip — make a fun, quick final photo before the airport.
options.food: Grab-and-go coffee and pastries on the way to the airport.

tip.label: Don't miss the flight
tip.body: Return the hire car with a full tank to avoid the refuelling surcharge, and leave a big buffer — LAS security queues are long. Passports, ESTAs and boarding passes ready before you leave the hotel.

bookings.name: Flights — LHR → San Francisco / Las Vegas → LHR
bookings.note: Six seats. Open-jaw: fly into SFO, home from LAS. Confirm seat allocation for the family together.

bookings.name: ESTA visa waivers ×6
bookings.note: One per traveller including the twins. Apply at least 72 hours before flying; print or screenshot the approvals.

bookings.name: Rental car — 7-seater SUV
bookings.note: 22-day hire, SFO pickup / LAS drop-off (one-way fee applies). Two booster seats for the twins.

bookings.name: Travel insurance — family policy
bookings.note: Full family cover including the theme-park and Grand Canyon activities and US medical.

bookings.name: Alcatraz cruise tickets
bookings.note: Day 3. Sells out weeks ahead — book as early as possible. Departs Pier 33.

bookings.name: Muir Woods parking / shuttle reservation
bookings.note: Day 4. Timed reservation mandatory — no turn-ups. Book the parking or the shuttle in advance.

bookings.name: Monterey Bay Aquarium tickets
bookings.note: Day 6. Dated online tickets are cheaper and skip the queue.

bookings.name: Hearst Castle tour
bookings.note: Day 8. Timed tour bus from the visitor centre — must be pre-booked.

bookings.name: Universal Studios Hollywood tickets
bookings.note: Day 12. Dated tickets; consider the Express pass for August crowds.

bookings.name: Disneyland tickets + park reservation
bookings.note: Day 15. Needs BOTH a dated ticket and a park reservation. Set up Genie+ the night before.

bookings.name: Six Flags Magic Mountain tickets
bookings.note: Day 17. Buy online in advance; the teens' day.

bookings.name: Grand Canyon West day tour
bookings.note: Day 21. Book the Skywalk / West Rim package and confirm the pickup or self-drive parking.

bookings.name: Las Vegas Raiders tickets
bookings.note: NFL game at Allegiant Stadium, Las Vegas — check the August fixtures fall within our Vegas dates (23–29 Aug) and book seats together.

packing.name: Passports & ESTA printouts
packing.note: All six, plus the car-hire and hotel confirmations. Keep together in one folder.

packing.name: Sun cream (high SPF) & hats
packing.note: Reef-safe, factor 50. The desert and the beach will both catch you out.

packing.name: Layers for the fog
packing.note: San Francisco and Big Sur are cold and windy even in August. A fleece and a light waterproof each.

packing.name: Reusable water bottles ×6
packing.note: Essential for the desert legs — refill everywhere. One each, labelled.

packing.name: US plug adapters & power bank
packing.note: UK→US adapters (a couple of multi-port ones), plus a power bank for the no-signal drives.

packing.name: Phone chargers & car charger
packing.note: Everyone's cable, plus a multi-port car charger for the long driving days.

packing.name: Swimwear & beach towels
packing.note: Quick-dry towels save space. Goggles for the pools and the sea.

packing.name: Comfortable walking shoes
packing.note: Broken-in trainers each — theme parks and canyon rims mean big step counts.

packing.name: Kids' entertainment
packing.note: Downloaded films, games and audiobooks for the flights and the long drives — offline, no signal needed.

packing.name: Medications & first-aid kit
packing.note: Any prescriptions in hand luggage, plus plasters, antihistamines, ibuprofen and travel-sickness tablets for the coast road.

costs.item: Attractions & tours (Alcatraz, Aquarium, Hearst, Grand Canyon)
